facts.text: Garrett Park was named for John Work Garrett, former B&O president who led the railroad during Civil War.
The town’s train station, built in 1893, still stands today and is the only B&O station in Montgomery County that survived.
In the 1920s, the Chevy Houses were sold with a brand‑new Chevrolet parked in the driveway, a quirky marketing trick still visible at Clermont Avenue.
The Garrett Park Historic District, listed on the National Register in 1975, preserves dozens of 19th‑century homes and the original train depot.
In 1977, Garrett Park declared itself an arboretum, keeping a detailed inventory of every town tree and a scheduled planting calendar.
The town incorporated in 1898 with just thirty buildings and about one hundred residents, a tiny but planned community from the start.
